lines.text: Stack blocks of granite, one on top of another.
The bottom one carries every block above it.
Squeeze granite with a hundred to two hundred and fifty million pascals, and it crushes.
That's a thousand to two and a half thousand times the pressure of the air around you.
Now build the tower as tall as Everest.
The pressure on the bottom block: about two hundred and thirty-five million pascals.
A tower of solid rock gives way somewhere between about four and nine kilometres.
lines.cue: caption: GIVES WAY AT ~4 TO 9 KM

lines.text: But Everest is taller than that, and it's standing right there.
So how does Everest stay standing? The full video on our channel shows the trick. Like and subscribe.
